title: M1 execution and control contracts v1

system_ref.description: SystemRef returned by put_system and accepted by get_system (system/records.md). Same id/sha256 pair as a Ref, but it names a system record, never a CC record.

trial_ref.description: TrialRef: resolves only to a controller-written rsi_trial in the private controller evidence root.

oracle_ref.description: OracleRef: resolves only through the oracle authenticated API.

launch_request.description: launch(prompt, channel, workspace) and POST /cc/runs. request_id is required: same id and same bytes return the same run (lost-response recovery), changed bytes give REQUEST_CONFLICT. seed is the requested nonnegative seed; headless maps to cc.execution.headless.

launch_result.description: Success is the services-v1 run_handle (run_id, run_dir, state, status_ref, manifest_ref). Rejection is the services-v1 error whose reason code names the cause: invalid intake or configuration exits 2, unavailable environment exits 4 (exit_code set 0, 2, 3, 4, shared with run_status_view and cli_json_output).

resume_request.description: resume(run_id, human_review_ref). human_review_ref names a committed human_review record whose action is resume_after_fix. Resume is terminal-only at M1.

abort_request_run.description: abort(run_id, human_review_ref) and POST /cc/runs/{id}/abort. Differs from services-v1 abort_request, which addresses a benchmark request id only. human_review_ref is required when the run is halted and may be omitted for a running run. Evidence is never erased.

run_status_view.description: RunView read by CLI, Web and TUI from GET /cc/runs/{id}. Rebuilt from committed records. planned_plan_ref is absent until freeze 2. exit_code, when present, is 0 completed, 3 halted or aborted, 4 environment unavailable (same set as launch_result and cli_json_output).

cli_json_output.description: JSON printed by cc status, inspect and doctor with --json; text output renders the same state. exit_code is the process exit code and uses the one closed set: 0 success or completed research (including a scientific FAIL), 2 invalid intake, configuration or arguments, 3 halted research, 4 unavailable environment, security or storage.

run_manifest.description: read_manifest(run_id): rebuildable closed view written only by the supervisor. Each step record is marked with its phase. planned_plan_ref is absent until freeze 2; an absent value is unavailable, never inferred success.

local_session_token.description: Contents of /run/jiuwenswarm/local-session.json (mode 0600): launcher to the in-container CLI.

vocabulary_ref.description: Vocabulary pin: id is the version name, sha256 the hash of its bytes.

record_input_request.description: record_input(run_id, type, vocabulary_ref, value | file, origin) from launcher or gate host to the runner. Exactly one of value and file_ref. The reply is the services-v1 ref of the written Artifact.

policy_ref.description: Policy pin: id is the epoch name, sha256 the hash of the epoch document.

vocabulary_ref.description: Vocabulary pin: id is the version name, sha256 the hash of its bytes.

freeze_request.description: freeze(run_id, validation_ref, policy_ref, vocabulary_ref) for one phase (launcher or supervisor to M03). validation_ref resolves to a committed plan_validation with status VALID and no findings.

commit_batch_manifest.description: manifest.json of DATA/cc/commits/<batch_id>/ (system/storage.md). The Ref of this manifest is what run_phase_started.batch_ref and workflow_start_args.pins_ref point to; resolve step_id to Binding ref through the entries.

freeze_result.description: Result of freeze: step_id to Binding ref map plus batch_ref, the Ref of the commit batch manifest that published all of them at once. An incomplete batch is never visible.

workflow_start_args.description: args of cc.adapters.swarmflow.start_run. The supervisor starts the same generic script once per phase. plan_ref is the run_plan control Artifact; pins_ref is run_phase_started.batch_ref (commit batch manifest of step_id to Binding ref). The planned phase also carries the prep release records so that prep.<step_id>.<port> sources resolve only to released outputs.

run_phase_started.description: System record for one freeze point (replaces run_started). Written once per phase by the supervisor after that phase's Bindings are committed as one batch: phase prep at launch (freeze 1, fixed prep plan: intent step then requirement step) and phase planned after the last requirement release (freeze 2, planner DAG validated and bound). id is run-phase-<run_id>-<phase>. payload.run_id equals the envelope run_id. batch_ref is the Ref of the commit batch manifest. A planned record carries the same library_snapshot_sha256 and the same effective_config_ref as the prep record; a mismatch is a conflict that halts. prep_release_refs lists the committed release records of every prep step and proposal_ref names the validated planner proposal. A dispatch_reserved for a prep step requires the prep record; for a planned node it requires the planned record.

dispatch_reservation.description: dispatch_reserved record, id dispatch-<dispatch_id>. dispatch_id is an id derived from the canonical tuple (run_id, step_id, binding_sha256, input content hashes, attempt); it is an opaque identity, not a content hash. Reserved before any effect. dispatch needs step_id and binding_ref; nested and gate need parent_obs_id and ordinal; admission uses session_id instead of run_id.

release_record.description: release record, id release-<dispatch_id>. Written by the supervisor only after authorize_advance re-read the committed Observation and Verification and found routing_action ADVANCE with verdict PASS or PASS_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.

human_review_record.description: human_review record written by the terminal adapter from an authenticated reply, fresh id. The envelope at is the review time.

system_record_lifecycle.description: Append-only lifecycle transition linked by previous_ref. A completed step requires release_ref (or experimental_advance_ref in an isolated experiment); halted requires reason.

system_record_planning_reserved.description: Reserved for the planner call after the last requirement release and before freeze 2. Payload is the services-v1 planning_reservation.

system_record_model_call_reserved.description: Reserved before the bridge forwards a model turn. Payload is the services-v1 model_call_reservation.

system_record_rsi_session.description: Offline RSI controller session state, a sequence linked by previous_ref. Parent, model, config, policy, evaluator and profile are immutable across the sequence.

system_record_rsi_trial.description: Immutable implementation snapshot of one RSI trial, written by the controller in its private evidence root. No hidden bytes.

system_record_rsi_security_clearance.description: Authenticated human request to clear an oracle security latch. It is permission to request clearance, not the latch transition itself.

system_record_oracle_session.description: Private oracle session, written by the oracle in its protected namespace. Private set hashes never cross into public controller records.

system_record_oracle_closure.description: Oracle closure record. Closing fixes zero to five ablations and has an empty result list; closed points to the closing record and the complete scheduled results.

system_record_oracle_result.description: Redacted aggregate oracle result. No per-case vectors, cases, outputs or set hashes. This exact immutable record supplies AggregateResult.result_ref.

system_record_oracle_security_block.description: Target-wide security latch keyed by incident ref. Append-only; cannot be erased to resume.

system_record_oracle_security_clearance.description: Written only by the oracle after human, custody and report validation. Restores the interrupted phase only, never quota.

system_record_oracle_quota.description: Private oracle quota reservation in its own protected root. Loop queries use session ordinal 1-30 and lifetime ordinal 1-90; final uses ordinal 1 and no lifetime ordinal. Uncertain queries are never refunded.

system_record_rsi_attempt.description: One closed Attempt entry (attempts.jsonl) owned by capsule/rsi-engine.md#attempt-record. attempt_id is the record id; previous_entry_sha256 links entries; no hidden cases.

system_record_activation.description: Library-scope activation written by the librarian. Neither run_id nor session_id is present. No run manifest mutates its library snapshot after activation.

system_record.description: SystemRecord union. Closed envelope {schema_version, kind, id, run_id?, session_id?, at, previous_ref?, payload}. kind selects exactly one variant; unknown kinds fail before publication. The old run_started kind is replaced by run_phase_started.

call_descriptor.description: The prompt the Swarmflow script sends to agent(): RFC 8785 canonical JSON of exactly these keys. Values travel by hash, control by reference: inputs are Artifact refs. The engine uses it only as a cache key; the supervisor dispatch identity authorizes reuse. A malformed descriptor is a protocol rejection with no Observation.

Present only for operation call. The caller (dispatch, nested, gate or admission), the parent obs_id and the ordinal are not fields of the request: they come from the dispatch reservation in reservation_ref.

runner_request.description: Supervisor to runner (decision D-b: the supervisor-side CcBackend calls the runner, then the Gate host). Frames are length-prefixed UTF-8 JSON (4-byte big-endian length), limited by cc.ipc.max_frame_bytes. Only call carries call_descriptor. The caller (dispatch, nested, gate or admission), the parent obs and the ordinal come from the reservation in reservation_ref, not from the request. cancel and status address the existing dispatch_id and never start work. The same dispatch_id with changed bytes is REQUEST_CONFLICT.

runner_response.description: Runner to supervisor. A complete response requires a durable Observation ref (outputs and capture are committed first). The call outcome (ok, error, refused) is read from the Observation, not from this state.

runner_event.description: Proposed RunnerEvent frame (observability gap 1): runner to supervisor, sent after the described record is written, so the supervisor-hosted bus can publish it.

step_envelope.description: ENVELOPE_SCHEMA (cc.adapters.swarmflow.ENVELOPE_SCHEMA): CcBackend to the engine, returned by agent() to the script. A cache only; it never authorizes release without the committed Verification and release record.

tool_host_frame.description: Length-prefixed frames (4-byte big-endian length, then one UTF-8 JSON object; max cc.ipc.max_frame_bytes, large values by ref) between the runner tool handler and the tool-kind child process (the tool host), over the inherited socket pair. t selects the frame. Tool host to runner: ready, nested (nested call), model (model request), issue, result, failure, unavailable, exception. Runner to tool host: call, nested_result, model_result. id is a counter local to the call and pairs requests with results. The optional obs_id is the proposed observability gap 2 correlation field. Check mode uses the same frames with no broker, so nested and model frames end the check unknown.

skill_turn_frame.description: The one JSON object a model must reply with in a skill turn (after optional code-fence removal): either outputs (keys equal the output port names exactly, optional issues) or one call to a pinned non-prompt_section capsule. Any other top-level key, or both outputs and call, breaks a parse rule and ends the call with CAPSULE_ERROR.

runner_turn_entry.description: One entry of Observation.ext.runner.turns, appended per model turn. request_id (the bridge request id) is the proposed addition from observability so that a bridge request joins to its obs_id.

model_client_call.description: The runner M05 complete(prompt, model_hint, session_id, deadline, context=ModelCallContext) call as data. It maps to services-v1 model_bridge_request as follows. scope -> scope. obs_id -> obs_id. turn -> turn. operation = turn and target_request_id = null. session_id -> session_id (fresh per turn, derived from the scope hash, request_id, obs_id and turn). model_id = model_hint when given, else the model_id of the reserved model_call_reservation. deadline_at -> deadline_at. prompt is first stored as scoped capture and its scoped_capture_ref becomes prompt_content_ref (namespace public_artifact for run, planning and admission scopes). request_id is allocated by the broker from the reservation. capsule_name, decl_hash, step_id and role stay local audit metadata and are never sent to the endpoint.

model_client_reply.description: M05 result as data: ModelReply on success, ModelError otherwise. Success is built from a model_bridge_result with state complete: the reply bytes come from reply_content_ref and are checked against reply_content_sha256; request_id is the bridge request_id; model_id, tokens and route_record_id come from the model audit record and are null when the runtime did not report them (Codex reports none). Error mapping: timed_out -> TIMEOUT; unavailable, denied, cancelled, or queued/running at the deadline -> RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE; a reservation or budget ceiling reached (BUDGET_EXCEEDED) -> BUDGET_EXCEEDED; an empty prompt (INVALID_INPUT) -> CAPSULE_ERROR. A cancelled turn is never a success.

gate_request.description: gate(obs_ref) (decision D-b: the supervisor-side CcBackend calls the runner, then the Gate host, after the runner committed the Observation). The Observation must have caller dispatch or nested; gate and admission callers are rejected to end referee recursion.

gate_result.description: GateResult returned by gate(obs_ref), computed once and read back from the committed Verification (its gate_result). verification_ref is null only for a cancelled call, which is blocked/ENVIRONMENT_BLOCKED. Fold: PASS and PASS_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATIONS are decision pass, normalized PASS, ADVANCE; FAIL is decision fail; ENVIRONMENT_BLOCKED is decision blocked, normalized BLOCKED; INCONCLUSIVE is decision blocked. M1 non-advancing outcomes use HALT or ESCALATE_TO_HUMAN (an action, not a verdict). The supervisor still re-reads the committed Verification before releasing.

halt_report.description: What the halt host reports to the human session (or prints in headless mode, which exits with code 3): failing step, exact Observation and Verification, reason and its owner, known durable evidence and permitted actions. A halt with no Gate verdict (gate-save failure, capture failure, invalid planned plan) omits verdict and verification_ref. Reading a report is not approval.

event_envelope.description: Events on the in-process cc event bus (cc.events.emit and subscribe), one variant per event name. Each carries run_id (or candidate_id at admission) and at. An event that describes a record is emitted after the record is written. cc.call.started, cc.call.resolved, cc.call.refused, cc.call.nested and cc.model.turn only announce. cc.run.frozen is emitted once per freeze (phase prep at launch, phase planned after requirements). cc.run.halted covers every halt, including halts with no Gate verdict. Events never carry authority; the committed records do.

evidence_manifest_ref.description: Return of seal_execution(obs_id, capture). manifest_path is workspace-relative, never absolute and never contains a .. segment.

execution_evidence.description: Return of get_execution(ref): the internal complete Stage Evidence Bundle manifest, not the bounded model-facing evidence_bundle. All relative_path values resolve under the bundle root. Missing required evidence is EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE or EVIDENCE_CORRUPT.

exit_code.description: Process exit code, one closed set for every command: 0 success or completed research (a scientific FAIL is still 0), 2 launch, intake or configuration rejected, 3 halted, 4 environment unavailable (security, storage or model auth).

dispatch_id.description: Identity of the reserved dispatch this commit belongs to.

content_ref.description: Staged bytes the runner wrote to its own staging area. The supervisor re-reads them, checks sha256 and commits.

refs.description: For kind capture: the staged capture parts, in order.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the canonical bytes to commit; equals content_ref.sha256.

commit_request.description: The runner asks the supervisor, over their authenticated channel, to commit an Observation, Artifacts or capture on its behalf. The runner holds no write access to the store (single writer per kind); the supervisor verifies run_id, dispatch_id and obs_id against the dispatch reservation, re-hashes the staged bytes and commits. Same request_id with the same bytes returns the same result.

commit_result.description: Reply to commit_request. committed carries the Ref of the stored record. refused (unknown dispatch, wrong run, hash mismatch, over the size limit) and conflict (same record id with different bytes: REQUEST_CONFLICT or STORE_CONFLICT) carry a reason and no ref. A refused commit is never retried automatically.
